newsitem.title: USA: N.Y sees 1998 Goodwill games enhancing Olympic bid.
newsitem.headline: N.Y sees 1998 Goodwill games enhancing Olympic bid.

text.p: New York said on Tuesday that the fourth Goodwill Games, which it will host in 1998, will let it prove that it is well-equipped to handle the summer Olympics even though they are a much bigger event.

In addition to the stature gained by hosting the Olympics, state and New York City officials have ample financial incentives to try to attract the summer games, a long-range goal that likely will require years of planning.

The 1996 summer games that were held in Atlanta pumped $4 billion into the state's economy and should give state and local governments $400 million more in revenues, according to the Economic Forecasting Center at Georgia State.
Gov. George Pataki was confident the state, which in 1980 hosted the winter Olympics in Lake Placid, will succeed in its drive to win the summer Olympic games.

"There's no question in my mind that we're going to show the world what we can do, the state, the city and Nassau County, working together in 1998. And after that there's no reason the world won't look to New York to come back and do something even bigger," he told reporters.
State officials said the Goodwill Games will mean "hundreds of millions" of dollars for the New York metropolitan region.
Mayor Rudolph Giuliani brushed aside perhaps the paramount chief concern about hosting the Olympics, providing security.

"You can never avoid the unexpected, but this is about as good a place to have an event like this as you can have it," he said, noting the city has lots of experience playing host to tourists and world leaders, as it did last year, when 150 dignitaries feted the 50th anniversary of the United Nations.

The 1998 Goodwill Games will be split between Manhattan and Long Island. Diving and swimming will be held at Nassau County's $24 million Aquatic Center, while gymnastics and indoor volleyball will take place at the Nassau Colliseum.

Basketball, boxing and figure skating will be played at New York City's Madison Square Garden, with cycling at Colombia University. Manhattan also will hold the triatholon, and beach volleyball will be played in Central Park.
